text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Malawi has been grouped among five African countries including Ghana, Mali, Mozambique and Uganda in the "New Partnership for Africa", an initiative to jumpstart African economies from their dependency syndrome, a visiting American Economist said in Lilongwe.

- Wage dispute talks between the government and civil servants initially due to egin on Thursday to negotiate the workers' demand for a 100 percent increase have been postponed to next week Tuesday because the leader of government negotiating tetam is unwell, Southern Malawi union leader Thomas Mwafongo said on Wednesday.
- Mob justice is increasing at an alarming rate and spreading to the villages, despite frequent pleas against it, police in Lilongwe said on Wednesday.

- Suspected supported of the ruling United Democratic Front (UDF) on Tuesday invaded an opposition Malawi Congress Party (MCP) by-election campaign rally in Chiradzulu, southern Malawi, doused people with petrol, and set ablaze the party's landrover motor vehicle.

- The Malawi Congress Party says it is concerned with the local radio's coverage of campaign news, charging the country's only radio is favouring the ruling United Democratic Front in the run-up to the May 26 byelections.
